newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Campus violence flares in S.Korea after Kim apology.
newsitem.headline: Campus violence flares in S.Korea after Kim apology.

text.p: Radical South Korean students demanding the resignation of President Kim Young-sam clashed with riot police on Tuesday, hours after Kim apologised over a loans scandal.
It was the first campus violence since a crackdown last year on student activism.

Police fired volleys of teargas at about 700 students hurling rocks and shouting "Down with the Kim Young-sam regime" at Seoul's Hanyang University, witnesses said. At least five students were detained.
Earlier, Kim apologised to the nation over a loans scandal involving the failed Hanbo Steel Co.
Students burned a coffin wrapped in black cloth to symbolise what they said was the death of democracy.
They were angry at government attempts to ram through parliament a controversial labour law and another piece of legislation beefing up a domestic intelligence agency.
Kim was forced to send both bills back to parliament after their passage on December 26 sparked a month of strikes.
The students also demanded an independent probe into the crisis at Hanbo Steel, which was declared insolvent on January 23 after piling up $5.8 billion of dubious loans.
Last August riot police stormed Seoul's Yonsei University to dislodge students occupying two teaching blocks in what authorities labelled pro-North Korean agitation.
